question: When you say you are 80% sure, are you right 80% of the time?
finding: A forecaster who says 90% every time and is right 70% of the time scores exactly 0.25, the same as answering 50% to everything; that is a property of the Brier score, and the made-up example log (80% confident, 71% right over 24 predictions, score 0.216) only illustrates it.
limit: The score depends on which questions you choose and on your own honesty in resolving them, and a few dozen forecasts are too few to separate skill from luck.
